conflicts: 4s 2P3/2 (74225.846 cm^-1): beam-foil lifetime 1.51(7) ns (Schectman et al. 1993) gives A(134.72 nm) = 5.64e+08 s^-1 and A(136.34 nm) = 9.78e+07 s^-1 (f = 0.153(11), 0.055(4)), about 35 per cent larger than the NIST ASD values 4.19e8 and 7.5e7 s^-1 (accuracy C+); the same paper lists earlier measurements f(1347) = 0.109(10) (Schwab & Anderson 1982), 0.10(3) (Clyne & Nip 1977), 0.113 (Lawrence 1967), 0.090 (Hofmann 1967).
4s 4P5/2 (71958.363 cm^-1): phase-shift lifetime 1.5 us +-15 per cent (Lawrence 1967) versus 4.3 us implied by the NIST ASD A = 2.3e5 s^-1 (accuracy D) of the 138.97 nm intercombination line.

2P1/2-2P3/2 interval: 882.3519(12) cm^-1 (Dagenais et al. 1976, isotope-weighted mean) versus 882.35283(23) (35Cl) / 882.35367(23) (37Cl) (Braun et al. 1982) versus NIST 882.3515; all agree within about 1 sigma of the older value. Isotope shift 37-35: +28.2(2.0) MHz (Dagenais) versus +25.2 MHz from the difference of Braun's two values.

Level naming around 91000-92000 cm^-1: the J = 5/2 level at 91343.50 cm^-1 is 5s 2[2]5/2 in NIST but is called 3d 2F5/2 by Alkhayat et al. 2019 (after Oliver & Hibbert 2007), whereas this file (after Schectman et al. 1993 and NIST) labels 91906.79 cm^-1 as 3d 2F5/2. Biemont et al. 1994 argue that the NIST labels of 91127.03 (3d 2D5/2) and 91906.79 (3d 2F5/2) should be interchanged. Entries are identified by energy; the labels are only names.
5s lifetimes: measured 5.83(36), 8.98(72), 6.28(18) ns (Alkhayat et al. 2019) vs 21.3, 17.8, 29.2 ns calculated by Ojha & Hibbert 1990 and 6.26, 8.07, 7.50 ns by Oliver & Hibbert 2013.

f(1090.73 A): 0.0095(8) from the beam-foil lifetime (Alkhayat 2019) vs 0.0028(4) from interstellar absorption (Sonnentrucker et al. 2006); the authors attribute the difference to blending in the stellar spectrum.

4s resonance lines: measured f values (Clyne & Nip 1977; Schwab & Anderson 1982; Hofmann 1967, quoted from Biemont et al. 1994) vs NIST ASD: e.g. 133.57 nm f = 0.028(6) -> A = 2.1e8 s^-1 (NIST 1.74e8), 118.877 nm f = 0.068(7) -> A = 2.1e8 s^-1 (NIST 2.33e8); for 137.31 nm (4P1/2) the measurements differ among themselves by a factor 2.5 (7.9(4.8)e-5 vs 3.2e-5). The second-hand measured values have 7-60 per cent uncertainties.

notes: Literature search was limited: the session's web-search quota was exhausted, so sources were located through Crossref, HAL, OSTI, arXiv and NASA ADS queries and only open copies could be read (APS, IOP, Elsevier, Canadian Science Publishing full texts were not accessible). Hyperfine constants of the ground term are second-hand from Chichinin's JPCRD review (method 'compilation'). Signs: A, B as printed (Casimir convention, E = A*C/2 + B*[...]). The M1 A value is the calculated one adopted by NIST. Values marked 'derived' were computed here from the quoted measured numbers. Two-photon entries: wavelength_vac_nm is the laser wavelength (two photons of that wavelength reach the upper level). Second pass (2026-10-01): beam-foil lifetimes of four more levels from arXiv:1910.05803; second-hand measured oscillator strengths of the 3p5 - 4s resonance lines read on the scanned Table 3 of Biemont et al. 1994 (NASA ADS; the image was checked by eye) and converted to A here (derived, method compilation). Lawrence-1967 entries in that table are listed only as alternatives because all but two of them come from an intermediate-coupling analysis of his lifetime measurements. Lines to 4s 4P levels are typed "intercombination".
